cut_items.item: Explicitly states that docker system prune also removes build cache and unused networks, and details what each category covers
Warns that running containers are not removed by the prune command, and gives a stop-then-force-remove sequence followed by prune to cover them
Notes that `--filter` can be used to narrow what is pruned
Lists `docker volume prune -a` in the per-type commands, which covers named volumes
States that docker system prune -a --volumes also removes build cache
Compact script to remove running containers too: docker stop, docker rm -f, then prune -f
Mentions a --filter option to control volume pruning (vague)

added_items.item: Full-reset path that removes all images and volumes by name: `docker rmi -f $(docker images -aq)` and `docker volume rm $(docker volume ls -q)`. These also delete named volumes.
Says the empty-list usage errors in the full-reset steps are harmless and the step can be skipped
Concrete backup method: run a temporary container that mounts the volume and archives it with tar
Says the anonymous-volume-only behavior of `--volumes` applies from Docker 23.0 onward
Says Docker keeps anything a running container uses when pruning
Says `-f` can be added to any prune command, and that Docker Desktop's disk image size lives under Settings > Resources
Says build cache can take many GB and recommends `docker builder prune -a`; this is also in X's per-type list, but X does not explain why
Advice to check what data exists first (docker system df) before running the destructive command, as a pre-step
Explicit step-by-step manual removal of everything: stop, rm, rmi -f, volume rm, with the note that empty-list usage errors are harmless
Explanation that -a removes all unused images, not only dangling ones, and that Docker keeps anything used by a running container
Note that docker system prune does not always clear build cache, so run docker builder prune -a separately; build cache can use many GB
Docker Desktop: specific Settings > Resources > Disk image size path as well as Clean/Purge data
How to back up a volume: run a temporary container mounting the volume and archive with tar
Warning that volumes often hold database data and the action cannot be undone
docker volume rm command for removing all volumes explicitly, and docker rmi -f for removing all images
